chapter_seo_title: The River Cleanses Chenyu - Ji Ning’s Destructive Rampage & Mu Northson’s Frenzy
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning tears through the Chenyu Mountains with the River Su, crushing Shaoyin formations while sparing mortals. Mu Northson loses control—will Ji Ning stop him before karmic hellfire strikes?
og_title: Desolate Era Ch. 448 – The River Cleanses Chenyu
og_description: Ji Ning’s rampage on Shaoyin territory, seen through the eyes of three young cultivators. A bittersweet clash of vengeance and mercy.
twitter_title: Desolate Era 448 – The River Su sweeps Shaoyin
twitter_description: Ji Ning destroys formations, Mu Northson goes berserk, and the mortal world watches in terror. A pivotal breather chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: The legendary river from Chinese mythology that flooded the earth during the time of the Great Yu. In Desolate Era, Ji Ning controls it as a devastating weapon and a tool of mercy.
A powerful technique unleashed by Mu Northson’s Yixian puppet, producing a storm of wind and thunder that annihilates everything in its path.
A cultivator who failed the Celestial Immortal tribulation and lost their physical body, surviving as a 'wandering' immortal who faces periodic tribulations.
A mystical flame that arises from the sin of killing mortals. It burns the soul from within, regardless of the cultivator's physical defenses.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Ji Ning spare the mortals but kill the cultivators?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Killing mortals incurs severe karmic sin that would make his tribulation nearly impossible to survive. Cultivators, being participants in the martial world, generate far less sin. Ji Ning has standards: he won't massacre the innocent, even in revenge.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why aren't the Shaoyin Loose Immortals fighting back?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They have been ordered by their Celestial Immortal ancestors to defend passively and conserve strength. They have already sent a message talisman to summon the ancestors. Engaging Ji Ning directly would waste lives without certainty of victory.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What will happen to Mu Northson if he kills mortals?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Killing mortals on a large scale would create a heavy cloud of karmic sin around him, which could trigger karmic hellfire during his tribulation. Ji Ning's warning is not just moral—it's a life-or-death issue in the Xianxia cosmology.
